title: JUDO: A Juxtaposed Domain-Oriented Multimodal Reasoner for Industrial Anomaly QA
claim: A staged training pipeline progressively injects visual context and domain knowledge into a model, turning a query into a grounded, reasoned answer.
layout: 4 columns left-to-right, color-coded stages, example outputs in boxes below
description: A wide, left-to-right figure with color-coded columns: Query (purple), Stage 1 (green), Stage 2 (cyan), Stage 3 (yellow). At left, a speech bubble holds a defect question with multiple-choice options, above a magnifying-glass icon. Stage 1 shows query and normal images of a cable on a mesh surface, feeding a 'Segmentation based Juxtaposed Reasoning' box. Stage 2 adds a domain snippet (book icon) and a domain question, feeding 'Domain Knowledge Injection'. Stage 3 shows stacked Segmentation, Domain Reasoning and Answer cards feeding a Reward box, plus a 'Domain-oriented GRPO' box. A smiling robot icon marks the output. Below each stage, a rounded pastel box in the matching color gives example text: ground truth, domain answer, pseudo-domain rationale, and generated output with seg, think and answer tags.
caption: Overview of \mname{} (Juxtaposed Domain-Oriented Multimodal Reasoner). The framework progresses in three stages: (1) Stage 1: Learning anomaly segmentation-based juxtaposed reasoning, (2) Stage 2: Domain-knowledge injection, and (3) Stage 3: Domain-oriented group relative policy optimization. Through the progressive stages, we incorporate the domain knowledge and context into LMMs for reliable and robust anomaly analysis.
abstract: Industrial anomaly detection has been significantly advanced by Large Multimodal Models (LMMs), enabling diverse human instructions beyond detection, particularly through visually grounded reasoning for better image understanding. However, LMMs lack domain-specific knowledge, which limits their ability to generate accurate responses in complex industrial scenarios. In this work, we present JUDO, Juxtaposed Domain-Oriented Multimodal Reasoner, a framework that efficiently incorporates domain knowledge and context in visual and textual reasoning. Through visual reasoning, our model segments the defect region by juxtaposing query images with normal images as visual domain context, enabling a fine-grained visual comparative inspection. Furthermore, we inject domain knowledge through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to enhance context understanding and subsequently guide domain reasoning through reinforcement learning (GRPO) with tailored rewards, opting for a domain-oriented reasoning process. Experimental results demonstrate that JUDO achieves superior performance on the MMAD benchmark, surpassing models such as Qwen2.5-VL-7B and GPT-4o. These results highlight the importance of enhancing domain knowledge and context for effective reasoning in anomaly understanding.
